sentiment_reasoning: Middle East escalation (UAE missile interception, Strait of Hormuz disruption) drove oil up 5% to $114 Brent and 10Y yields to 4.46%, hammering risk assets Monday. Tuesday futures bounce modestly but the energy/inflation cocktail keeps the Fed in pause mode and pressures duration-sensitive growth names. Defense and energy outperformance masks broader index weakness; sentiment skews bearish with tactical longs in tankers, defense, and integrated oil.

summary.gist: Iran-UAE missile exchange has shut traffic through the Strait of Hormuz and lit oil markets on fire - Brent at $114 is the highest since 2022 and is doing the Fed's hawkish work for it. Trade the dispersion, not the index.

executive_summary: Risk assets remain caught between Middle East escalation and a Fed unwilling to ease into oil-driven inflation. Monday's tape: Dow -1.13%, S&P -0.41%, Nasdaq -0.19%, Brent +5% to $114. Tuesday futures show modest bounce (S&P +0.27%, Nasdaq +0.4%) but breadth is poor and defensive sectors lead. The macro setup favors energy, defense, and shipping over consumer discretionary, airlines, and long-duration tech. AMD reports after close - the most-watched semi print of the week. With Fed at 3.5-3.75% and 10Y at 4.43%, every leg higher in oil makes the Fed's job harder.

macro_events.title: Iran-UAE missile exchange shuts Strait of Hormuz traffic
macro_events.causal_chain: UAE intercepts Iranian missiles + Fujairah oil hub fire -> most shipping ceases Hormuz transit -> Iraq/Saudi/UAE shut in production -> 21% of global oil and 20% of LNG flow disrupted -> war-risk insurance premiums on VLCCs spike -> Brent/WTI spread widens -> Asian refiners reroute via Cape of Good Hope (+12-14 days, +$2M/voyage) -> Qatar LNG to Europe at risk -> Dutch TTF gas futures higher -> US 10Y yield rises on inflation expectations to 4.46% -> Fed cut probability collapses -> equity multiple compression in long-duration assets
macro_events.geographic_dimension: Persian Gulf supply concentration: Saudi 9.8mb/d, UAE 3.0mb/d, Iraq 4.5mb/d, Iran 3.4mb/d, Kuwait 2.7mb/d; Hormuz also carries 90Mt/y Qatar LNG to global markets
macro_events.historical_analog: Sep 2019 Abqaiq drone attack: Brent +15% in 24h, mean-reverted within 3 weeks once Saudi capacity restored. Current setup more durable - multi-state supply disruption vs single-asset 2019
macro_events.counterargument: US announced naval escort plan and Iran reviewing peace proposal; ceasefire optionality could collapse risk premium overnight. SPR releases could blunt 5-10% of price spike
